claims.text: The degree of local lattice distortion governs the superconducting transition temperature in superconducting high-entropy alloys.
Random atomic-size mismatch induces local lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortion tunes Tc by changing electron-phonon coupling strength.
An as-cast random BCC refractory HEA with substantial atomic-size disparity has associated lattice strain.
Annealing can reduce local lattice distortions without changing the alloy's overall composition.
Enhanced chemical short-range order is associated with reduced local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions modify the phonon spectrum.
Changes in the phonon spectrum modify electron-phonon coupling channels.
Atomic-size differences create local stress fields and lattice distortions.
The local stress fields and distortions soften specific phonon modes.
Softening of specific phonon modes enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling can increase Tc.
Annealing-induced relief of distortion alters the local phonon density of states and thereby modulates Tc.
The more highly distorted as-cast alloy is expected to have a higher or more spatially inhomogeneous Tc than the annealed alloy.
Tc and superconducting-gap uniformity should vary systematically with the measured degree of lattice disorder.
The proposed mechanism is expected to be significant in BCC HEAs with substantial atomic-size mismatch.
The effect of local lattice distortion on superconductivity may be minimal in low-size-disparity alloys or FCC HEAs.
Disorder-related impurity scattering may compete with the Tc-enhancing effect of stronger electron-phonon coupling.
